s: The Indian influence in Seychelles is noticeable in the use of spices, curry, cinnamon, vanilla, chilli, and many more, waiting for you in the market stalls. The same goes for tea, another day-to-day protagonist of the lives of the inhabitants of the islands. In the market of Sir Selwyn-Clarke there is also a great variety of spice and tea stalls, also in Victoria Market, where besides souvenirs, you can buy fresh fruits and fish and taste the rich cuisine of the country.
